svg.data-weight: 32 kg fully loaded (two REs, two LMICs); 16 kg without FRUs (Table 22)
svg.data-depth-with-brackets: 782 mm over cable-management brackets, air filter and handles (Table 22)
svg.data-throughput: 4.8 Tbps system capacity; up to 12x400 Gbps or 48x100 Gbps ports (three LMICs)
svg.data-storage-temp: -40 C to 70 C in shipping container
svg.data-asic: Juniper Trio 6 (one YT ASIC per LMIC)
svg.data-macsec: inline MACsec on all ports at all speeds
svg.data-timing: 1PPS and 10 MHz SMB input and output, ToD and BITS RJ45, GM/PTP SFP (1-GbE/10-GbE); BITS and GM/PTP currently reserved for future use per the guide
svg.data-redundancy: full hardware redundancy - Routing Engines, power supplies and fans

The rear carries two stacked 2200 W PSUs (AC, DC, or HVAC/DC), a fixed timing strip (1PPS and 10 MHz SMB in/out, ToD, BITS, and a GM/PTP SFP), three fan modules and the earthing terminal.","format":1,"gaps":[{"reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["res","lmics","psus"],"wanted":"a mechanical drawing resolving the module envelopes against the drawn apertures - Table 22 states 203.5 mm module and 73.5 mm PSU envelopes while the photographed apertures measure 197.6 and 66.0; the bays and module faces are both drawn at the aperture and the envelopes live in each contract's attrs. the router requires two power modules for 1+1 redundancy"},"index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"PSU"},"res":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"1+1","redundancy-note":"1+1 - mx304 hardware guide, \"MX304 Component Redundancy\": \"Routing Engines-A redundant system consists of two Routing Engines which are available as field-replaceable units (FRUs). One Routing Engine functions as the primary and the other functions as the backup. If the primary host subsystem (or either of its components) fails, the backup takes over as the primary. The Routing Engine installed in slot 0 functions as the default primary Routing Engine.\" The form assumes the second bay holds a Routing Engine; on this chassis that bay can instead take a third LMIC, in which case the router runs on one RE and there is no redundancy to state"},"description":"Routing Engine slots - RE 0, and RE 1/LMIC2 which accepts a Routing Engine or a third LMIC. Positions are photo-fractions, approximate","chassis":"datasheet-table - Table 22: chassis 3.5 x 17.36 x 24.01 in (88.9 x 440.8 x 610 mm), 2RU; 78.2 cm deep over cable-management brackets and handles. The chassis-description prose says 17.63 in (44.8 cm) wide - a 0.7 cm disagreement with Table 22; the table is carried and the prose recorded here. Fully loaded 32 kg, bare 16 kg. Ears are NOT MODELLED by project convention; the modelled body is the 440.8 mm between the flange folds, and the slot labels (RE 0, LMIC0, RE1/LMIC2, LMIC1) are printed on the REMOVABLE BRACKETS the photographs show, so they appear nowhere on this body - recorded so their absence is not read as an omission","color":"photo - medium grey chassis (#8b8f94), bright aluminium module plates, pale blue ejector levers, Juniper orange fan furniture","esd":"guide Figure 11 (ESD Points) - one point on the front badge strip top, one on the rear right above the earthing plate. Both are plain sockets in the photographs","fan-strips":"photo - each fan bay's chassis strip to its right prints the fan icon, the bay number and the bicolour status lamp (Table 12: green blinking = hardware init complete, green steady = ok, yellow steady = faulty). The fourth strip position at the far right shares the ground zone","front-cover":"not modelled - the optional front cover with air filter (JNP-FLTRDR-2RU + JNP-AIRFLTR-2RU, Table 22) bolts over the entire front face; the guide documents replacement procedures for both. Modelled configuration is the bare front as photographed; see gaps","grounding":"guide grounding specifications + photo - two threaded holes for M6 pan-head screws on 16 mm centres at the rear right, under the earth symbol; the protective earthing terminal bracket attaches here. Modelled as juniper/mx304-ground-plate","lifecycle":"none-announced - searched \"Juniper MX304 end of life end of sale\" 2026-08-26; the third-party EOL trackers list no dates and the 2022 NANOG thread names the MX304 as the successor replacing the MX204 and MX10003. Absence of the announcement is the finding","other-faces":"near-blank by evidence - no source shows the top, bottom or side faces; each carries only an estimated mounting-rail band so the capability chain counts it as drawn, sized from Table 22. Axis conventions per viewer3d.js: LEFT view x = 0 is the REAR, RIGHT view x = 0 is the FRONT, top and bottom y = 0 at the FRONT","power":"guide Table 25, the vendor's own per-module table at two ambients for the 3.2 Tbps two-RE + two-LMIC 100GbE configuration: REs 49/59 W each, SFB+CB+PMB 155/228 (chassis internals, not a FRU here), LMICs 318/410 each with transceivers, fans 48/90 each; total chassis power 1033 W at 25 C and 1436 W at 46 C. Those totals are carried as the device figures with that scope in power-envelope; Table 26 gives the 400GbE configuration and its totals fell outside this extraction's text layer - not carried rather than guessed","rear":"photo (mx304-rear-ac-high) - stacked PSU bays at x 10.9 (PSU 0 above PSU 1, labels printed vertically on the chassis strip right of them), the fixed timing strip at 84-116, three 82.0 mm fan bays EVENLY spaced at x 116.4, 225.4 and 334.5 (26.9 mm label strips between and after, each printing the bay's number, lamp and fan icon), and the earthing plate and rear ESD socket at the right end. A FIRST READING PUT FAN 1 AT 213.4 AND CALLED THE SPACING ASYMMETRIC - it had mis-assigned fan 1's edges to its grille internals; the DC rear photograph (independent shot, same chassis) and a zoom on the strip between fans 1 and 2 both give the even layout, and the reviewer's instinct that routers do not stagger their fans was what triggered the re-measure. The rear drawing (g101368 family) was measured too but its verticals mix module internals at this threshold and were not used for positions","scale":"photo + drawing, cross-anchored per axis - the guide front drawing (g101366) measures aspect 5.58 against the rack face's 5.43 and is internally inconsistent in x by ~1.5%, and the front photograph is ~16% COMPRESSED in y (near-axis studio shot) while consistent in x. So: front x positions come from the photograph at 4.058 px/mm anchored to the 440.8 body, front y positions from the drawing anchored to the 88.9 height. The rear photograph is near-isotropic (3%) and rear positions come from it at 4.236 px/mm (x) / 4.106 (y). Feature sizes come from the registry and Table 22 throughout","slots":"drawing + photo - four half-width apertures in two columns of two: RE 0 above LMIC 0 on the left, RE 1/LMIC2 above LMIC 1 on the right (guide Figure 2 callouts name all four). Rows y 4.1-43.8 and 44.6-84.3 off the drawing; columns x 1.2-198.8 and 205.3-402.9 off the photograph, separated by the centre rail. A one-RE system may seat a THIRD LMIC in the RE 1/LMIC2 slot (guide Figure 3 shows it; hardware overview text: \"You can also add a third LMIC into one of the Routing Engine slots\"). The 197.6 mm apertures take 203.5 mm module envelopes - the modules carry insert: for the difference","sources":"MX304 Universal Routing Platform Hardware Guide (figures g101366/ g101368/g101334/g101624 among others, extracted with captions into working/images/mx304/), MX304 datasheet (mx304-datasheet.pdf), Juniper image-library studio photographs mx304-front-high, mx304-rear-ac-high and mx304-rear-dc-high, and the NetBox devicetype-library MX304 elevations. No mechanical drawing was available","timing":"photo + guide timing topic - SMB quad at x 98.6/107.1, y 11.6/22.2 (rows 10 MHz above 1PPS, columns OUT left / IN right per the rotated legends), BITS RJ45 centred at 101.9, 35.6, ToD at 101.3, 55.4, and the GM/PTP SFP cage VERTICAL at 100.1, 74.9 with its link lamp to the left.
